fact: Ooredoo Algeria's CEO says it takes part in the government-led Universal Telecommunication Service project to extend mobile coverage to remote and underserved areas, aiming to deploy more than 1,200 rural sites.
Minister Zerrouki said a project of 1,400 new mobile sites was launched for low-profitability zones, with the state subsidising operators in areas under 2,000 inhabitants.

The minister launched the universal-service project on 21 October 2024 with 4G networks lit in Djelida and El Amra (Ain Defla), part of 91 Ain Defla localities in Ooredoo's share of 1,400 zones, 760 new antennas.

Two ministerial arretes of 6 June 2024, published in JO no. 45, award the universal-service mobile coverage lots for low-density localities to Wataniya Telecom Algerie (83 lots) and Optimum Telecom Algerie (13 lots).
The Minister of Post and Telecommunications told the APN a new universal-service programme covers 1,400 zones under 2,000 inhabitants, with operator offers being studied by ARPCE before execution.
